mainTopic: Offerings that come להכשיר: why the עומר and the אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע are פסול שלא לשמן, and רבי ירמיה's distinction between מכפרים and מכשירים
overview: The amud opens at the end of a statement about offerings that have a special job. It says a מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is פסולה. It also says an אשם נזיר or אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמן is פסול, because they came להכשיר and failed. The גמרא asks why our משנה does not list the עומר among its exceptions. It answers that the משנה deals only with individual, independent מנחות that have no fixed date. Next, the גמרא asks why the opening משנה of זבחים does not list these two guilt offerings. It answers that other kinds of אשם are כשר, so the משנה could not list 'אשם' as one blanket exception. The גמרא then asks why making fit should differ from atoning. רבי ירמיה answers that the Torah separates מכפרים from מכשירים: only מכפרים can be brought after the owner's death, as shown by the woman after childbirth. רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי objects from a משנה where a dead נזיר's עולה and שלמים are still brought. רב פפא answers that רבי ירמיה meant only a fixed הכשר, and the נזיר's offerings are a non-fixed הכשר. The explanation of why the נזיר's offerings count as non-fixed continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The leper's guilt offering is also disqualified
steps.stepSummary: The statement continues: an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמו is פסול, because it was meant to make the person fit and it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same applies to the guilt offering of a מצורע: if they were slaughtered not for their own sake, they are disqualified. This is because they came to make the person fit, and they did not make him fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement it began just before this. Certain offerings that have a special job become פסול if they are done שלא לשמן, and here the אשם מצורע is added to that group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an offering done שלא לשמו is still כשר, even though the owner does not get credit. The אשם of a נזיר and of a מצורע are different, because their whole purpose is להכשיר, to make the person fit again. If they are slaughtered for the wrong purpose, they fail at that job, so they are פסול completely.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering brought by a person healed from צרעת as part of his purification
Not for their own sake: offered with the intention of being a different kind of offering
Disqualified, invalid
To make fit: here, allowing the person to return to full status, such as eating קדשים

phrases.english: And the guilt offering of a leper,
that one slaughtered them not for their sake, they are disqualified,
since they came to render fit,
and they did not render fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement begun before this section about offerings that come to permit or to make fit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם מצורע (like an אשם נזיר) slaughtered שלא לשמו is פסול, because it failed to make the owner fit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This statement sets up the whole sugya. Offerings with a specific job (להתיר or להכשיר) are treated more strictly than ordinary offerings done שלא לשמן.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה list the עומר as an exception?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה, which lists only מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות as exceptions. If the עומר is also פסול שלא לשמה, it should have been listed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: all meal offerings from which a handful was taken not for their sake are fit, but they do not count for the owner's obligation, except for the sinner's meal offering and the meal offering of jealousy. If the statement is true, let the משנה also teach: 'except for the עומר meal offering'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the earlier statement, made just before this amud, that a מנחת העומר done שלא לשמה is פסולה. If that is true, why didn't our משנה include the עומר in its list of exceptions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a general rule: מנחות done שלא לשמן are כשר. It names only two exceptions, מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות. A list of exceptions is expected to be complete, so leaving out the עומר suggests the עומר follows the general rule and is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A קמיצה, a handful of flour, was taken from them to be burned on the מזבח
They do not count toward the owner's obligation
The meal offering a poor sinner brings in place of an animal
The meal offering of a סוטה, a woman suspected by her husband
The barley meal offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits eating the new grain
And if it is so: if that statement were true

phrases.english: We learned: All the meal offerings
from which a handful was removed not for their sake are fit,
except that they did not go up for the owner
as an obligation,
except for the meal offering of a sinner and the meal offering of jealousy.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the earlier statement is right that the עומר becomes disqualified when done for the wrong purpose.

phrases.english: let it also teach: 'Except for the omer meal offering'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement that a מנחת העומר done שלא לשמה is פסולה
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a מנחת העומר whose קמיצה was done שלא לשמה is פסולה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's list of exceptions does not include the עומר. That suggests the עומר follows the general rule and is כשר.

steps.title: The משנה only lists individual offerings
steps.stepSummary: First answer: the משנה's list deals only with מנחות brought by an individual. The עומר is a communal offering, so it is not part of the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches its list, it teaches offerings that come from an individual. It does not teach offerings that come from the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The משנה was never trying to discuss communal מנחות, so the עומר's absence proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two exceptions the משנה names are both brought by a single person. The עומר is brought on behalf of the whole community. The list is complete for individual offerings, so the absence of a communal offering does not show that it is כשר שלא לשמה.

keyTerms.meaning: Comes from an individual: a private offering
Comes from the community: a public offering
When it teaches: limiting what the משנה was dealing with

phrases.english: When it teaches, it is about one that comes from an individual;
one that comes from the community it does not teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by narrowing the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's list covers every kind of מנחה, so the עומר should have been included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה deals only with individual offerings, and the עומר is communal.

steps.title: The משנה only lists meal offerings brought on their own
steps.stepSummary: Second answer: the משנה deals only with מנחות that are brought by themselves. The עומר is brought along with an animal offering, so it is outside the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches its list, it teaches a meal offering that comes on its own account. It does not teach one that comes on account of an animal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another reason why the משנה might leave out the עומר. The משנה only discusses independent מנחות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The עומר is brought together with a lamb offering, so it is tied to a זבח. The משנה's list covers only מנחות that stand by themselves. This is a separate way to limit the משנה, not the same point as the individual-versus-community answer.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of itself: an independent offering
On account of an animal offering: brought together with it

phrases.english: When it teaches, it is about one that comes on account of itself;
one that comes on account of a slaughtered offering it does not teach.
phrases.notes: The עומר is brought together with a lamb, so it fits this description.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent way to limit the משנה and answer the same קשיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every מנחה is included in the משנה's list.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list covers only independent מנחות, and the עומר comes with a זבח.

steps.title: The משנה only lists offerings without a fixed date
steps.stepSummary: Third answer: the משנה deals only with מנחות that have no set time. The עומר has a fixed date, so it is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה teaches its list, it teaches those that have no fixed time. One that has a fixed time it does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a third reason why the עומר is missing from the משנה. The עומר has a set date, and the משנה only discusses offerings with no fixed time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מנחת חוטא and מנחת קנאות can be brought on any day. The עומר may only be brought on the 16th of ניסן. Since it is a different kind of offering, the משנה did not include it. That keeps the earlier ruling, that the עומר is פסול שלא לשמה, standing.

keyTerms.meaning: Has a fixed time: may be brought only on a set date
Those: the offerings the משנה does list

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list of מנחות that are פסול שלא לשמן is not a complete list of all מנחות. It covers only individual, independent offerings with no fixed date. So the עומר can be פסול שלא לשמה without contradicting the משנה.

phrases.english: When it teaches, it is about those
that have no fixed time;

phrases.aramaic: הָא דְּקָבוּעַ לָהּ זְמַן – לָא קָתָנֵי.
phrases.english: this one, which has a fixed time, it does not teach.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the עומר, which is brought only on the 16th of ניסן.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָתָנֵי הָנָךְ שֶׁאֵין קָבוּעַ לָהֶן זְמַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third way to limit the משנה and answer the same קשיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה should list every מנחה that is פסול שלא לשמה, including ones with a fixed date.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה lists only offerings with no fixed date, and the עומר has one.

steps.title: Quoting the rule about the nazirite's and leper's guilt offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the earlier statement that an אשם נזיר and an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמן are פסול, so that it can examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: In the same way, an אשם נזיר and an אשם מצורע that were slaughtered not for their own sake are disqualified, because they came to make the person fit and they did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting a line from the earlier statement again. This is a setup: it is getting ready to challenge it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most offerings slaughtered שלא לשמן still count as kosher offerings. This statement says these two are different. They are not about atonement. They are the last step that makes the נזיר or the מצורע fit again, and an offering brought for the wrong purpose cannot do that job.

keyTerms.meaning: The guilt offering a נזיר brings after becoming impure, so he can start his נזירות again
The guilt offering a healed מצורע brings as part of becoming pure and fit
To make someone fit or permitted
Disqualified, invalid as offerings

phrases.english: The Master said:
And so you say regarding the guilt offering of a nazirite
and the guilt offering of a leper, that if one slaughtered them
not for their sake, they are disqualified,
since they came to make the person fit
and they did not make him fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עומר discussion and goes back to the second part of the original statement, about the guilt offerings
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אשם נזיר and an אשם מצורע slaughtered שלא לשמן are פסול, because their job is to make the person fit and they failed to do it.

steps.title: The משנה in זבחים lists only פסח and חטאת as exceptions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says all offerings slaughtered שלא לשמן are valid except פסח and חטאת. If the אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע are also פסול, the משנה should have listed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: All offerings slaughtered not for their sake are valid, but they do not count toward the owner's obligation. The exceptions are the פסח and the חטאת. If the statement is true, the משנה should also say: except for the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע, since they came to make fit and did not make fit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the statement from step 6 using the opening משנה of זבחים, which gives a list of exceptions that does not include these two guilt offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to give a complete list of offerings that become פסול שלא לשמן, and that list has only two items. If these two kinds of אשם were also פסול, the list would be missing them. So the משנה seems to disagree with the statement.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not count for the owner as fulfilling his obligation, so he must bring another
The Passover offering
The sin offering
And if it is so, meaning if the statement is correct
Let it teach, meaning the משנה should have said it

phrases.english: We learned in a mishnah:
phrases.notes: This is the very first משנה of מסכת זבחים.

phrases.english: All offerings that one slaughtered not for their sake
are valid, except that they did not count
for the owners as fulfilling their obligation,
except for the Paschal offering and the sin offering.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the statement in step 6 is right.

phrases.english: let it also teach:
except for the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper,
since they came to make fit and did not make fit!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: כׇּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁשְּׁחָטָן שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמָן כְּשֵׁרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just quoted in step 6
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע are פסול שלא לשמן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in זבחים gives an exceptions list with only פסח and חטאת. Leaving out these two guilt offerings suggests they are valid.

steps.title: The משנה could not list אשם, because other kinds of אשם are valid
steps.stepSummary: Other guilt offerings, אשם גזילות and אשם מעילות, come for atonement and stay valid שלא לשמן. So 'אשם' is not one clean category the משנה could list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there are also the guilt offering for robbery and the guilt offering for misusing holy property, which come to atone, the rule about אשם is not clear-cut, so the משנה did not mention it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה only lists whole categories. Not every אשם is פסול, so 'אשם' could not be listed as an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פסח and חטאת are פסול שלא לשמן in every case. אשם is mixed: the נזיר's and the מצורע's are פסול, but the robbery and holy-property ones are valid. Because the משנה only lists rules that apply across a whole category, it left אשם out completely. That does not mean the נזיר's and מצורע's are valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Guilt offering brought for falsely swearing that one did not steal or owe money
Guilt offering brought for using holy property for personal benefit
Atonement
It is not clear-cut for him, meaning the rule does not apply across the whole category

steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע are valid. It only explains why the משנה did not mention them: the general heading 'אשם' covers kinds that are valid and kinds that are not.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of לָא פְּסִיקָא, that a משנה only lists clean categories, is a common way the גמרא explains why something is missing from a list.

phrases.english: Since there is the guilt offering for robbery
and the guilt offering for misuse of holy property,
which come for atonement,
it is not clear-cut for him.
phrases.notes: Since not every אשם is פסול, the תנא could not write 'except for אשם' as one blanket rule.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא אֲשַׁם גְּזֵילוֹת וַאֲשַׁם מְעִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the משנה in זבחים
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the list is incomplete: the משנה lists only categories that are uniform
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Leaving out the two guilt offerings means they are valid שלא לשמן
steps.terutzMaskana: They are פסול, but the category אשם is mixed, so the משנה could not list it as an exception

steps.title: Why should 'making fit' be different from 'atoning'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reason itself: the robbery and holy-property guilt offerings also failed at their job of atoning, so why aren't they פסול too?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the אשם נזיר and the אשם מצורע, that they are disqualified because they came to make fit and did not? The others also came to atone and did not atone!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the reason behind the statement. If failing to do the offering's job makes it פסול, the atonement guilt offerings should be פסול too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 8 depended on a difference between 'making fit' and 'atoning'. The גמרא asks why that difference should matter: in both cases the offering did not do what it was brought to do. The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks why two similar cases are treated differently
These too
They did not atone

phrases.aramaic: מַאי שְׁנָא אֲשַׁם נָזִיר וַאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע,
phrases.english: What is different about the guilt offering of a nazirite and the guilt offering of a leper,
that they are disqualified because they came to make fit and did not make fit?
These too
phrases.notes: He means the robbery and holy-property guilt offerings from the step before.

phrases.english: came for atonement and did not atone!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא אֲשַׁם נָזִיר וַאֲשַׁם מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the distinction that step 8 relied on, between offerings that make fit and offerings that atone
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason 'they came to make fit and did not make fit' as a special ground for being פסול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Failing to atone is just as much a failure of the offering's purpose as failing to make fit, so both kinds of אשם should be treated the same.

steps.title: Offerings that atone versus offerings that make a person fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that the Torah itself separates מכפרים from מכשירים: מכפרים can come after the owner's death, but מכשירים cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: We find that the Torah made a difference between offerings that atone and offerings that make a person fit. Some atoning offerings can be brought after the owner dies. No fitness offerings can be brought after the owner dies.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה answers the question from Step 9. He explains why the robbery and holy-property guilt offerings are treated differently from the אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אשם גזילות and אשם מעילות are מכפרים: they atone for a sin. The אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע are מכשירים: they make a person fit again, so the נזיר who became impure can start his נזירות over and the מצורע can eat holy food. רבי ירמיה says the Torah is stricter with מכשירים, so it makes sense that only they become פסול שלא לשמן.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings that bring atonement for a sin
Offerings that make a person fit again, for example to eat holy food or drink wine
After death, meaning brought after the owner has died
The Torah made a distinction

steps.whyThisMatters: This מכפרים / מכשירים split becomes the key idea that the rest of the discussion tests.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
We find that the Torah made a distinction
between those that atone and those that make fit,
phrases.notes: "Make fit" is the אשם נזיר and אשם מצורע. "Atone" is the robbery and holy-property guilt offerings from Step 8.

phrases.english: those that atone, there are among them
some that come after death,
those that make fit, there are none among them
that come after death.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצִינוּ שֶׁחִלֵּק הַכָּתוּב בֵּין מְכַפְּרִים וּבֵין מַכְשִׁירִין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every guilt offering that failed to do its job should be פסול in the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: מכשירים are a stricter category than מכפרים, so only they become פסול שלא לשמן.

steps.title: Proof from the woman who died after childbirth
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that heirs bring a woman's עולה, which atones, after her death, but not her חטאת, which makes her fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If a woman brought her sin offering and died, her heirs bring her burnt offering. If she brought her burnt offering and died, her heirs do not bring her sin offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה brings a משנה to prove his rule that מכשירים are not brought after death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After childbirth, a woman brings a חטאת and an עולה. In this case the עולה counts as atoning, so the heirs may still bring it after she dies. The חטאת is what makes her fit, so once she has died, it is not brought.

keyTerms.meaning: Her sin offering, here the one that makes her fit after childbirth
Her burnt offering, here the one that atones
Heirs

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה:
A woman who brought her sin offering and died,
the heirs shall bring her burnt offering;
her burnt offering and died,
the heirs shall not bring her sin offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבי ירמיה's distinction
steps.raayaObject: מכשירים are not brought after the owner's death, but מכפרים can be
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in קינים about a woman after childbirth

steps.title: Challenge: fitness offerings are also brought after death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי questions the claim that מכשירים never come after death. He begins quoting a משנה about money set aside for a נזיר's offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי objected: Is it really true that no fitness offerings come after death? But we learned in a משנה: If someone sets aside money for his נזירות offerings, one may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה, because all of it could end up as peace offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא attacks רבי ירמיה's rule. He starts quoting a משנה that he will use as his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge targets the second half of רבי ירמיה's rule, that מכשירים never come after death. The opening lines of the משנה set up the case of a נזיר's money. The part that actually matters comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Objected to it, attacking a stated view
His nazirite vow, here meaning the offerings he brings at its end
Liable for מעילה, misusing holy property
Peace offerings

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda objected to it,
son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi:
Those that make fit too,
are there really none among them
that come after death?
But didn't we learn in a משנה:
One who sets aside money for his nazirite offerings:
one may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for misuse,
because all of it is fit to be brought as peace offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that מכשירים never come after death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about a נזיר will show fitness offerings being brought after the owner has died.

steps.title: The rest of the משנה: a נזיר who died
steps.stepSummary: If the נזיר dies, money already set aside for his עולה and שלמים is still used to bring those offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died and had money that was not divided up, it goes to communal gift offerings. If the money was divided up: the money for the sin offering is thrown into the Dead Sea, and there is no benefit and no מעילה. With the money for the burnt offering, a burnt offering is brought, and there is מעילה. With the money for the peace offering, a peace offering is brought. It is eaten for one day and does not need the loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the משנה. This is the part that will power the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the נזיר's death, his money set aside for an עולה and for שלמים is used to bring those exact offerings. Only the חטאת money is destroyed. This sets up the point that some מכשירים are brought after death.

keyTerms.meaning: Money set aside without saying which offering it is for
Money already assigned to specific offerings
Communal gift offerings
The Dead Sea, a place to destroy money that cannot be used

steps.raayaObject: מכשירים can be brought after the owner's death
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מעילה about a נזיר who died

steps.title: The punchline: the נזיר's offerings come after death
steps.stepSummary: The עולה and שלמים of a נזיר are מכשירים, yet the משנה has them brought after he dies, which contradicts רבי ירמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the burnt offering and peace offering of a נזיר are fitness offerings, and still they are brought after death!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה spells out his challenge clearly. Here are מכשירים being brought after the owner's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's עולה and שלמים are what allow him to drink wine again, so they count as מכשירים. Yet the משנה says they are still brought after he dies. That directly contradicts רבי ירמיה's rule that מכשירים are never brought after death.

keyTerms.meaning: But look, used to point out a contradiction
They are

steps.whatToRemember: רבי ירמיה said מכשירים never come after death, based on the woman after childbirth. The משנה about a נזיר seems to show מכשירים (his עולה and שלמים) that do come after death.

phrases.english: But the burnt offering and peace offering of a nazirite
are offerings that make fit,
phrases.notes: They make the נזיר fit to drink wine again.

phrases.english: and yet they come after death!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עוֹלָה וּשְׁלָמִים דְּנָזִיר דְּמַכְשִׁירִים נִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the contradiction out of the quoted משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's rule that מכשירים never come after death
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The נזיר's עולה and שלמים are מכשירים, yet the משנה has them brought after his death.

steps.title: רב פפא limits the rule to a fixed הכשר
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רבי ירמיה only meant that a fixed הכשר is never brought after death. The נזיר's offerings are a non-fixed הכשר, so they are no contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what רבי ירמיה means. We never find a fixed way of making someone fit that is brought after death. The נזיר's offerings are a way of making him fit that is not fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רבי ירמיה by narrowing his rule to a 'fixed' הכשר and placing the נזיר's offerings outside it. The sentence ends with a comma, because the גמרא is about to explain why the נזיר's הכשר counts as not fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רבי ירמיה meant every מכשיר is never brought after death. רב פפא says the rule covers only a הכשר קבוע, an offering that is the one set way to make the person fit. Since the נזיר's עולה and שלמים are a הכשר שאינו קבוע, bringing them after his death does not break the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed הכשר: the one set offering that must be brought to make the person fit
A non-fixed הכשר: an offering that makes the person fit, but is not the single required way
We do not find. It states a rule based on what never happens in the Torah's laws
After death, meaning after the owner of the offering has died

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא does not say the נזיר's offerings are not a הכשר at all. They are still a הכשר. They are just a non-fixed kind, so they fall outside רבי ירמיה's rule.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:

phrases.notes: 'Fixed' means it is the one set offering that must be brought to make the person fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב פפא הכי קא אמר רבי ירמיה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 by reinterpreting רבי ירמיה's rule from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the rule: רבי ירמיה's principle is limited to a fixed הכשר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי ירמיה meant that no מכשיר of any kind is ever brought after death, so the נזיר's offerings would contradict him.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a fixed הכשר is never brought after death. The נזיר's offerings are a non-fixed הכשר, so the משנה about the נזיר does not contradict רבי ירמיה.
